patterns.usage_note: Marks a result that contradicts what the first clause led you to expect, usually coloured with dissatisfaction, regret, or surprise (毎日水をやるのに花が咲かない); the first clause states something established, not a hypothesis. くせに needs one shared, criticizable person, while のに contrasts two different subjects or none at all. Left at the end of a sentence it becomes a sigh of regret (来てくれればよかったのに).

examples.ruby: 部屋[へや]はこんなに寒[さむ]いのに、弟[おとうと]は窓[まど]を開[あ]けたがる。
examples.english: The room is freezing, and yet my little brother keeps wanting to open the window.

examples.ruby: 毎日[まいにち]水[みず]をやるのに、この鉢[はち]の花[はな]は咲[さ]かない。
examples.english: I water it every day, and still the flowers in this pot won't bloom.

examples.ruby: 約束[やくそく]の時間[じかん]を過[す]ぎたのに、電車[でんしゃ]はまだ来[こ]ない。
examples.english: The scheduled time has come and gone, and the train still isn't here.

glosses: when all it would have taken was …
patterns.usage_note: Voices exasperation or regret that an easy better course was not taken: a clause naming what would have sufficed, then ものを (素直に謝れば済むものを). It typically follows a conditional 〜ば / 〜たら and often ends the sentence, leaving the actual outcome unspoken. のに can report a plain contradiction with no blame attached; ものを always carries the complaint. もんを is its spoken contraction.

examples.ruby: 素直[すなお]に謝[あやま]れば済[す]むものを、彼[かれ]は言[い]い訳[わけ]を並[なら]べた。
examples.english: A simple apology would have settled it, and instead he reeled off excuses.

examples.ruby: 一言[ひとこと]相談[そうだん]してくれれば、金[かね]の工面[くめん]はできるものを。
examples.english: If he'd said one word to me, I could have scared up the money.

examples.ruby: 早[はや]めに出[で]れば間[ま]に合[あ]うものを、妹[いもうと]はぎりぎりまで寝[ね]ていた。
examples.english: Leaving early would have got her there in time, and my sister lay in bed till the last second.

patterns.usage_note: Marks a situation that the following clause then cuts against, in two uses: the inconvenience a request, apology, or thanks imposes (お忙しいところを恐れ入りますが), and a departure from the normal course of things (普段なら三十分で着くところを). のに and ものを carry the speaker's dissatisfaction, while ところを states the situation without it. It belongs to ceremonious speech and written narration.

examples.ruby: お忙[いそが]しいところを、わざわざお越[こ]しいただき恐縮[きょうしゅく]です。
examples.english: I'm much obliged to you for coming all this way when you're so busy.

examples.ruby: 普段[ふだん]なら三十分[さんじゅっぷん]で着[つ]くところを、二時間[にじかん]も要[よう]した。
examples.english: A trip that would normally take half an hour ended up taking two full hours.

examples.ruby: 実費[じっぴ]を請求[せいきゅう]できるところを、先方[せんぽう]は無償[むしょう]で応[おう]じた。
examples.english: They would have been within their rights to bill us for costs, yet they handled it free of charge.
